transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because I'm just... losing hours, lately. To rechecking things. Just everyday stuff, like door locks or my dressing supplies... and work things, too, like file dimensions and revision notes. 

I just... I don't feel allowed to just move on. I end up going through the same routine over and over, enough times until... I don't know, until the anxiety finally drops. So... yeah. That's what brings me in.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Yeah... I guess so. It's just... well, even when I know I've already cleaned a wound area, or... reviewed a CAD file for work... this thought just keeps cutting in. 

Like I missed one tiny thing. And... that it's going to turn into an infection, or a design mistake that ends up hurting somebody. I try to just reason it away, but... I can't really do that. It just stays there.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks or routines in a very specific way?

Yeah... um, I guess. Like I was saying before, it's... it's a routine. I just have to go through it a certain way. 

If I don't do it right, or if I try to rush it... I just don't feel allowed to move on. The anxiety won't drop unless I do it exactly like that. So... yeah.
Do you have any disturbing images or pictures that come into your mind?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't think I see pictures or anything like that. It's mostly just... the thoughts I mentioned before.
Are you trying to prevent something bad from happening when you do these checks or routines?

Yeah... I guess so. I just don't want those bad things to happen. But... it's taking up a lot of my day. 

I end up losing hours just... rechecking things. The door locks, my dressing supplies... and at work, it's the file dimensions, or revision notes. I just... I don't feel allowed to move on until I've gone through the routine enough times. Just... until the anxiety drops.
Are you doing these checks to reduce your anxiety or to actually prevent something bad from happening?

Um... I guess both. Like I was just saying, I... I just can't move on until the anxiety drops. If I don't repeat the routine with the locks or my files enough times, that feeling just stays there. So... I guess I'm mostly just doing it to make that stop.
Do you feel like you have to perform physical actions, like touching or tapping, in a certain way to reduce your anxiety?

Um... no, not tapping or... touching things in a special way. Just... like I mentioned before, it's the rechecking. Physically going through the same routine with the locks, or my supplies... I just have to do it enough times. That's... that's really it.
Are these repetitive thoughts and checking behaviors affecting your relationships or work performance?

Yeah... I guess they are. At work, I've... I've been missing some deadlines lately. I just end up staying late, trying to... get comfortable enough with the files to actually submit them. And, um... outside of work... I don't really go to my paddleboarding meetups anymore. Or work out. By the time I get through the routines, I just... I don't have the time left for that stuff.
Are your repeating thoughts mostly about something bad happening to yourself or to others?

Um... mostly others, I guess. Like... with the CAD files at work, I... I know I reviewed them. But this thought just cuts in that I missed something tiny, and... someone's going to get hurt because of a design mistake. Or... like if I have a small cut, I know I cleaned it, but I just keep thinking I missed a spot and it's going to get infected. I... I can't just reason it away. It just stays there.
Do you feel like things need to be symmetrical or just right, in addition to being checked repeatedly?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't really care if things are lined up or symmetrical. It's just... the checking. That's all.
Are your repeating thoughts and checking behaviors focused on preventing specific types of harm, like injury or illness?

Yeah... I guess so. Just... like what I mentioned before. People getting hurt from the designs, or... getting sick from a cut. I don't really know what else to call it. I just... don't want those things to happen. That's pretty much it.
Do you feel like these repeating thoughts are unwanted and coming into your mind against your will?

Yeah... they are. I don't want them there. Like I was saying before... even after I know I’ve cleaned a wound, or I know I reviewed a CAD file, the thought just cuts in anyway. It just tells me I missed one tiny thing and it’s going to turn into an infection, or... a design mistake that hurts someone. I don't invite it. I try to reason it away, but... I can't. It just forces its way in.
Do you feel like these thoughts are a part of you or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?
Um... I don't know. They're my thoughts, I guess. I mean... I'm the one having them. They don't feel like... someone else putting them there, if that's what you mean. Just... my brain getting stuck.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are necessary to prevent harm from occurring to others?

Yeah, I mean... I guess that's the idea. It's just... that's kind of what brought me in. I'm losing hours just... rechecking things. Like the file dimensions at work, revision notes... door locks, my dressing supplies. I just... I don't feel allowed to move on to the next thing until I've gone through the same routine enough times. Just... until the anxiety drops. So... yeah. I guess I feel like I have to.
Do you feel like these thoughts are inconsistent with your own values or beliefs?
I don't really know. Um... I haven't thought about it like that. They're just... things I worry about. I'm not sure if it has anything to do with my beliefs.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are aimed at directly preventing harm from happening?

Um... I mean, kind of like I said before. I guess so. But mostly it's just... I have to do the routines. With the doors, or my work files. I just do it until the anxiety drops. If I don't check enough times, I just... I don't feel like I'm allowed to move on to the next thing. I don't know if I'm always thinking about a specific harm, I just... have to do it.
Are your repeating thoughts mostly about harm from something specific like germs, contamination, or something else?

Um... I guess it's specific things. Like... with my dressing supplies, I'll clean the wound area, and I know I did, but... this thought just keeps cutting in. Like I missed one tiny spot and it's going to get infected. Or at work, with a CAD file... I'll review it, but I just keep thinking I missed a small detail and it's going to cause a design mistake that hurts someone. I just... I can't seem to reason it away.
Do you feel like you would be responsible if something bad happened to someone as a result of your mistake?
I... I guess so. Yeah. If I messed up the file, or... if I didn't clean the wound right, it would be my fault. I mean... I'm the one doing it, so... yeah.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are a way to avoid feeling guilty if something bad were to happen?
I don't know... maybe? I try not to think about it like that. I just... I just don't want anything bad to happen.
Do you think your checking behaviors are partly because you couldn't live with yourself if something bad happened as a result of your mistake?
I... I don't really know. I guess I haven't really thought about it that deeply. I just... I just want to make sure things are done right.
